IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.claim: A common construction omits a possessive head noun, promotes its dependent noun into its place, and assigns the verb to that dependent.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r1.anchor: من ذلك: أن تحذف المضاف وتقيم المضاف إليه مقامه وتجعل الفعل له.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r17.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r17.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r17.claim: Let him call his council means let him call his people.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r18.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r18.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r18.claim: He begins another ellipsis pattern: one verb is applied to two things though it belongs to only one, with a suitable verb understood for the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p133/r18.anchor: ومن ذلك أن توقع الفعل على شيئين وهو لأحدهما، وتضمر للآخر فعله.

ITQAN:v3p101/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p101/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p101/r5.claim: Conversely, a place can stand for its occupants; hand for power, heart for intellect, mouth for tongue, and town for its inhabitants.
ITQAN:v3p101/r5.anchor: الرابع عشر عكسه نحو ﴿ فليدع ناديه ﴾ أي أهل ناديه أي مجلسه ومنه التعبير باليد عن القدرة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Abu Jahl challenged the Prophet while he prayed and boasted of his powerful assembly, the verses threatening to summon the guards were revealed; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.anchor: فقال أبو جهل إنك لتعلم ما بها ناد أكثر مني فأنزل الله ﴿ فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال الترمذي حسن صحيح

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r12.claim: Falyadʿu means Abu Jahl should summon the people of his meeting; “nādī” requires an omitted “people” because the place itself cannot be summoned.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r12.anchor: أبو جهل {ناديه} أي أهل ناديه ومجلسه ليعينوه وهو المجلس الذي ينتدى فيه القوم

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r13.claim: Dar al-Nadwa was the Meccan place for consultation and is now a gathering hall of the Hanafi school.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r13.anchor: ودار الندوة بمكة كانوا يجتمعون فيها للتشاور وهي الآن لمحفل الحنفي

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.claim: Abu Jahl once challenged Muhammad while he prayed and boasted that he had the largest council in the valley; the answer threatens him with the punishment angels.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.anchor: روى أن أبا جهل مر برسول الله وهو يصلي فقال ألم ننهك فاغلظ رسول الله فقال أتهددني وأنا أكثر أهل الوادي ناديا يريد كثرة من

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.claim: Let him summon his council; God will summon the Zabaniya and command them to destroy him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.anchor: فليدع أهل ناديه وأهل مجلسه ، وسندعو الزبانية ونأمرهم بإهلاكه

TUSTARI:96:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:96:17/r1.claim: The council refers to a person's clan or kin group.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl confronted Muhammad as he prayed at the Maqam, threatened him, and boasted that he had the largest council; the verses answer his threat to mobilize his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي والنسائي عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.claim: The council is first the place where people assemble; it is called a council only while its members are gathered, and its daytime gathering contrasts with the nighttime “sāmir”.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.anchor: اسم للمكان الذي يجتمع فيه القوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.claim: Qusayy established a Quraysh council house around the Sacred Mosque for consultation and major affairs; the site was gradually incorporated into later mosque expansions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.anchor: واتخذ قصي لندوة قريش دارا تسمى دار الندوة حول المسجد الحرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r1.claim: “Council” also means the people who gather there: Abu Jahl means the many people who sit with him as their leader, just as place-names can denote inhabitants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r1.anchor: ويطلق النادي على الذين ينتدون فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r2.claim: The metonymic usage of a place for its people is supported by poetic uses of “majlis,” “maqāmāt,” and “majāmiʿ” for those who occupy them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r2.anchor: نظير إطلاق المجلس على أهله في قول ذي الرمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r3.claim: The command to summon his council is a taunting challenge: if Abu Jahl calls them to attack, God will call angels to destroy them; the challenge was a Quranic miracle because neither Abu Jahl nor his supporters dared act.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r3.anchor: للتعجيز لأن أبا جهل هدد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكثرة أنصاره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r4.speaker: أعرابية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p451/r4.claim: An Arab woman praised a man as the master of his council and the support of those in need.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r13.claim: “Let him call his council” points to Abu Jahl's boast that he had the largest gathering in the valley; nadi means an assembly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r13.anchor: وقوله: فليدع ناديه إشارة إلى قول أبي جهل، وما بالوادي أكثر ناديا مني،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r14.speaker: زهير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r14.claim: Zuhayr's poem uses andiya for meeting places, supporting the lexical meaning of council or assembly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502#2/r14.anchor: والنادي والندى المجلس ومنه دار الندوة ومنه قول زهير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r1.speaker: زهير والأعرابية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r1.claim: The poems and an Arab woman's expression use nadi for a gathering place or its leader, continuing the lexical evidence for Abu Jahl's boast.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r1.anchor:
وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم ... وأندية ينتابها القول والفعل
ومنه قول الأعرابية: سيد ناديه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reads “let him call to his council.”

AKHFASH:v2p582/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p582/r2.claim: Nādīhi means his clan, since they are the people of the gathering place; al-nādī itself is the place and meeting council.
AKHFASH:v2p582/r2.anchor: ها هنا عشيرته وانما هم اهل النادي والنادي مكانه ومجلسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet in prayer; after the Prophet rebuked him, Abu Jahl boasted of his clan, prompting the warning to call his assembly and the promise of the guards of Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل فقال ألم أنهك عن هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#2/r1.claim: The people of the assembly are the man's companions gathered there; he is told to call on them for help.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#2/r1.anchor: أي أهل ناديه وهم أهل مجلسه فليستنصرهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.claim: Abu Jahl is challenged to summon his clan for help, while God will summon the angels of punishment to show which party prevails.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.anchor: {فليدع ناديه} أي: قومه وعشيرته، أي: ليدعهم يستنصر بهم، {سندع الزبانية} وهم ملائكة العذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him pray at the Kaaba; the Prophet warns angels would seize him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن على عنقه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl confronting the Prophet at the Maqam and boasting of his large assembly; the verses were revealed, and Ibn Abbas says the angels would take him immediately if he called them. Al-Tirmidhi grades this hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل بن هشام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.claim: In another report from Ibn Abbas, Abu Jahl threatens to step on the Prophet's neck; the Prophet says angels would seize him visibly if he did. The report also warns that people challenging the Prophet would face loss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت رسول الله يصلي عند الكعبة لآتينه حتى أطأ على عنقه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad for praying at the Maqam, verses about the forelock, his council, and the angels were revealed; the Prophet prayed and Abu Jahl saw troops between them. Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he moved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه. فأنزل الله، عز وجل:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl swearing to trample Muhammad while he prayed; as he approached he recoiled, describing a trench of fire, terror, and wings. The Prophet says angels would have snatched him limb by limb; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation context was part of Abu Hurayra's report. Ibn Kathir says Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit it through Mu'tamir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يصلي

FARRA:v3p278/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r11.claim: His nādī is his people: Arabs use council, assembly, gathering, or witness for a man’s group.
FARRA:v3p278/r11.anchor: والعرب تقول: النادي يشهدون عليك، والمجلس، يجعلون: النادي، والمجلس، والمشهد، والشاهد- القوم قوم الرجل،

FARRA:v3p278/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r12.claim: A poet’s description “they have a council …” attests majlis for the assembled people.
FARRA:v3p278/r12.anchor:
قوم الرجل، قال الشاعر .
لهم مجلس صهب السبال أذلة ... سواسية أحرارها وعبيدها

FARRA:v3p279/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r5.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p279/r5.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh adds ilā before nādiyah and uses fa-sa-adʿū for “then I will call.”
FARRA:v3p279/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: «كلا لئن لم ينته لأسفعا بالناصية» ، وفيها: «فليدع إلي ناديه فسأدعو الزبانية»

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#5/r1.claim: His nādī means the people of his assembly whom he would call to help him; nādī itself is a council or meeting place.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#5/r1.anchor: {فليدع ناديه} أهل ناديه؛ أي ينتصر بهم. و "النادي": المجلس. يريد: قومه.

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r6.claim: A nādī originally is a gathering place for people who confer, then came to mean any assembly.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r6.anchor: والنادي: مجلس أهل الندى، فهذا أصله، ثم كثر فسمي كل مجلس ناديا.

JISHUMI:v10p7481/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r6.claim: In another account Abū Jahl threatened to fill the valley with cavalry and men; “let him call his council” was revealed, and the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb if he approached.
JISHUMI:v10p7481/r6.anchor: لأملأن عليك إن شئت هذا الوادي خيلا جردا ورجالا مردا، فنزلت: (فليدع ناديه)

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r2.claim: His nādī means followers and council members whom he summons in crises; they can only witness his shared calamity and cannot help.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r2.anchor: فليدع ناديه أي: أتباعه وأهل مجلسه، وكانوا يستغيثون بهم في الحوادث

KASHSHAF:96:17/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:17/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:17/r1.claim: Nadi means a meeting place, while the intended meaning is the people who gather there.
KASHSHAF:96:17/r1.anchor: والنادي : المجلس الذي ينتدى فيه القوم

KASHSHAF:96:17/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:17/r2.speaker: جرير
KASHSHAF:96:17/r2.claim: Jarir's line about a council of red-haired men illustrates the gathering-place sense.
KASHSHAF:96:17/r2.anchor:
كما قال جرير :
لَهُمْ مَجْلِسٌ صُهْبُ السِّبَالِ أَذِلَّةٌ ***

KASHSHAF:96:17/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:17/r3.speaker: زهير
KASHSHAF:96:17/r3.claim: Zuhayr's line illustrates that maqamat means gathering places.
KASHSHAF:96:17/r3.anchor:
وقال زهير :
وَفِيهِمْ مَقَامَاتٌ حِسَانٌ وُجُوهُهُمْ ***

KASHSHAF:96:17/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:17/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:17/r4.claim: A report says Abu Jahl challenged the Prophet during prayer and boasted he had the largest gathering in the valley; the verses followed.
KASHSHAF:96:17/r4.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل مرّ برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r6.claim: The nadi is the council where people gather, but the intended meaning is its attendees.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r6.anchor: والنادي : المجلس الذي ينتدى فيه القوم . أي : يجتمعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r7.speaker: جرير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r7.claim: Jarir's line uses majlis for a gathering place, poetic evidence for nadi.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r7.anchor: قال جرير : لهم مجلس صهب السهال أذلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r8.speaker: زهير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r8.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses muqamat for gathering places, another poetic parallel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r8.anchor: وقال زهير : وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r9.claim: Abu Jahl passed the Prophet at prayer, claimed he had forbidden him, threatened him, and boasted of his large following, prompting revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r9.anchor: أن أبا جهل مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

MAJAZ:v2p304/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p304/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p304/r5.claim: Nādiya means the people of one’s gathering or assembly.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r3.claim: The nadi is a gathering place associated with hospitality and generosity; calling its people means calling one's clan or supporter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r3.anchor: والنادي مجلس أهل الندى والجود ومعنى ( فليدع ناديه ) أي فليدع أهل ناديه من عشيرة أو نصير .

MUJAHID:v2p772#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p772#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p772#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the “assembly” is Abu Jahl’s clan.
MUJAHID:v2p772#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ فليدع ناديه ﴾ يعني عشيرته يعني أبا جهل

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r5.claim: Abū Jahl's supporters and gathering are Banū Makhzūm.

MUQATIL:96:17-19/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:17-19/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:17-19/r1.claim: The gathering means a supporter, and the zabāniya are the keepers of Hell, with their feet in the lowest earth and heads in the sky.
MUQATIL:96:17-19/r1.anchor: يعني خزنة جهنم أرجلهم في الأرضين السفلى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.claim: Nadi is the gathering place and means its people; zabaniya are the punishment angels, a word for enforcers derived from pushing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.anchor: ﴿ فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية ﴾ النادى المجلس الذى يجتمع فيه القوم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.claim: A report says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet during prayer, the Prophet rebuked him, and Abu Jahl boasted that he had the largest assembly in the valley; the Prophet warned that the angels would seize him if he called them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.anchor: روى أن أبا جهل مر بالنبى عليه السلام وهو يصلى

NAHHAS:v5p261/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r20.claim: The genitive head is omitted and its dependent stands for it: the people of his club.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r20.anchor: حذف المضاف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه اتساعا أي أهل ناديه

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r1.claim: The word nadi means Abu Jahl's gathering and clan, whom he is invited to call for support.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r1.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه وعشيرته، فليستنصر بهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r11.claim: Nadi is the meeting place where people gather, but here it means the people of the meeting place, as in the poetic citation.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r11.anchor: والنادي في كلام العرب: المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم أي يجتمعون،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r1.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r1.claim: Jarir's line about a council of gray-whiskered, submissive men gives poetic evidence for nadi as a meeting assembly.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r2.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r2.claim: Zuhayr's line about fine-looking stations or assemblies provides another poetic example for the gathering-place sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r2.anchor: وقال زهير: وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses majlis as the place where people meet and contend after Kulaib's death.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخر: واستب بعدك يا كليب المجلس

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r4.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r4.claim: Zuhayr's line about a neighbor and the man invited to the gathering shows nadaytu can mean to sit with someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18#2/r4.anchor: وقد ناديت الرجل أناديه إذا جالسته. قال زهير: وجار البيت والرجل المنادي

QUTB-ZILAL:96:17/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:17/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:17/r1.claim: The arrogant man may think to call on the family and companions in whom he takes pride for support.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:17/r1.anchor: فقد يخطر له أن يدعو من يعتز بهم من أهله وصحبه

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.speaker: الروايات الصحيحة
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.claim: Sound reports say all but the surah's opening passage was revealed about Abu Jahl after he saw Muhammad praying at the Maqam and forbade him.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r2.anchor: وردت بعض الروايات الصحيحة بأن السورة - عدا المقطع الأول منها - قد نزلت في أبي جهل

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.claim: Qutb suggests this may be the occasion when the Prophet seized Abu Jahl by the collar and rebuked him; Abu Jahl replied by boasting of his powerful council.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.anchor: وقال له : أولى لك ثم أولى فقال : يا محمد بأي شي تهددني

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had Abu Jahl called his council, the angels of punishment would have seized him immediately.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس لو دعا ناديه لأخذته ملائكة العذاب من ساعته

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.claim: While the Prophet prayed, Abu Jahl threatened him; his boast about having the largest gathering occasioned the summons of his assembly and the zabaniya, who would seize him if he summoned them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.claim: After the Prophet rebuked Abu Jahl and recited these verses, Abu Jahl boasted of his large assembly of dependents; this prompts the challenge to summon it and God's counter-summons.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.anchor: قال : يا محمد بمن تهددني وأني لأكثر هذا الوادي ناديا

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r8.claim: Al-Nadi means the people of a gathering, not the place itself, which is only called a gathering when its people are present; it derives from people resorting and assembling, as at Mecca's Dar al-Nadwa.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : ناديه أي أهل مجلسه

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r9.claim: Another derivation calls it the gathering of generosity; the phrase sarcastically invites Abu Jahl to summon his supposed noble, generous defenders.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r9.anchor: وقيل : سمي ناديا لأنه مجلس الندى والجود

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.claim: One reading dares Abu Jahl to call his supporters against Muhammad, while God summons zabaniya beyond his people's power; Ibn Abbas says they would seize him immediately, and other readings place his dragging in this world at Badr or in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.anchor: الأول : أي فليفعل ما ذكره من أنه يدعو أنصاره ويستعين بهم في مباطلة محمد

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says that if Abu Jahl summoned his assembly, the zabaniya would seize him at once, visibly.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية من ساعته معاينة

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.claim: An alternative reverses the order: God will seize the forelock and summon the zabaniya in the afterlife, so Abu Jahl may then call his assembly to try to stop them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.anchor: القول الثاني : أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا أي لنسفعا بالناصية وسندع الزبانية في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.claim: The fāʾ in ‘let him summon his assembly’ signals a miracle: the challenge invites the unbeliever to call them, which would trigger God's counter-summons; his failure to dare shows the Prophet's miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.anchor: الفاء في قوله : { فليدع ناديه } تدل على المعجز

SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r1.claim: Nādiyahu may delete a noun, meaning the people of his council, or figuratively summon the council itself because it contains people, like asking the village in 12:82.
SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r1.anchor: إما أن يكون حذف مضاف، أي: أهل ناديه أو على التجوز في نداء النادي لاشتماله على الناس

SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r2.claim: Nādī and nadī mean a gathering place for conversation; Zuhayr's reference to councils witnesses the usage.
SAMIN-DURR:96:17/r2.anchor:
والنادي والندي: المجلس المتخذ للحديث. قال زهير:
4609 وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم
وأندية ينتابها القول والفعل

TAB:96:18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:18/r1.claim: The nādī is Abu Jahl's gathering, supporters, relatives, and tribe; it means the council or meeting place.
TAB:96:18/r1.anchor: فليدع أبو جهل أهل مجلسه وأنصاره ،   من عشيرته وقومه ،   والنادي :  هو المجلس

TAB:96:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:18/r2.claim: After Muhammad rebuked him for stopping prayer, Abu Jahl boasted of having the largest council; God answers that He will summon the zabāniya if he persists.
TAB:96:18/r2.anchor: لأن أبا جهل لما نهى النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة عند المقام ،   انتهره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   وأغلظ له ،   فقال أبو جهل :  علام يتوعدني محمد

TAB:96:18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad at the Maqam; the Prophet rebuked him, and Ibn ʿAbbas says angels would seize him if he called his group.
TAB:96:18/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام ،   فمرّ به أبو جهل بن هشام

TAB:96:18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r4.claim: In another account, Abu Jahl says his council is greatest; the narrator does not remember Muhammad's reply, but Ibn ʿAbbas says angels would take him if he acted.
TAB:96:18/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي ،   فجاءه أبو جهل ،   فنهاه أن يصلي

TAB:96:18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:96:18/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts Abu Jahl's oath to trample Muhammad, his sudden retreat before a trench of fire and wings, and the Prophet's warning that angels would seize him limb by limb.
TAB:96:18/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  هل يُعَفّر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟

TAB:96:18/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad if he prayed again; black ranks appeared between them, and angels would have seized him had he moved.
TAB:96:18/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه ،   فأنزل الله

TAB:96:18/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that angels would have visibly seized Abu Jahl if he tried to trample the praying Messenger.
TAB:96:18/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة

TAB:96:18/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses nādī as Abu Jahl's supporter.
TAB:96:18/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله :  {  فَلْيَدْعُ نادِيَهُ } يقول :  فليدع ناصره

TAB-FULL:v24p537/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r2.claim: The command is for Abu Jahl to summon his assembly and clan supporters; nādī means the gathering place.
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r2.anchor: فقال أبو جهل: علام يتوعدني محمد وأنا أكثر أهل الوادي ناديا؟ فقال الله جل ثناؤه: {لئن لم ينته لنسفعا بالناصية} [العلق: 15]

TAB-FULL:v24p537/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r3.claim: The threat responds to Abu Jahl boasting that his assembly was the largest in the valley; if he summons it, God will summon the angels of punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p537/r3.anchor: عن داود بن أبي هند، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام، فمر به أبو جهل بن هشام

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat, his sudden retreat from a trench of fire, awe and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would tear him apart; the passage gives the revealed sequence.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قال: فقيل: نعم، قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the prayer place; when Muhammad prayed, Abu Jahl saw dark battalions between them and would have been seized by angels.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.anchor: عن الوليد بن العيزار، عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه، فأنزل الله:

TAB-FULL:v24p540/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the assembly Abu Jahl should call as his supporter.
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فليدع ناديه} [العلق: 17] يقول: «فليدع ناصره»

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r8.claim: Nādī means the council or meeting place, and here likely the people who gather there; the command is a challenge to summon them for help.
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r8.anchor: النادي المجلس وكأن المراد به أهل المجلس أي الجمع الذي يجتمع بهم

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r9.claim: An alternative takes nādī to mean an individual companion or fellow-sitter.

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r6.claim: His nādī means the people at his gathering or his clan, whom he is challenged to call for support.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r6.anchor: معناه فليدع أهل ناديه، وهم أهل مجلسه، وكانوا عشيرته أي فليستنصر بهم.

TABRISI:96:2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r6.claim: Al-nadi originally means the gathering place of the council's people, then came to mean any gathering.
TABRISI:96:2/r6.anchor: النادي مجلس أهل النادي ثم كثر فسمي كل مجلس ناديا

TABRISI:96:2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r14.claim: In 'let him call his gathering', people is elided after gathering: the intended meaning is the people of his council.

TABRISI:96:16-19/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:16-19/r4.claim: The threat means Abu Jahl may call his council's people and clan to help him when God's punishment comes; nadi can also mean an open courtyard.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r4.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه يعني عشيرته فليستنصر بهم إذا حل عقاب الله به والنادي الفناء

THALABI:v10p246/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p246/r6.claim: When Abū Jahl forbade prayer and was rebuked, he threatened to summon cavalry or footmen; the Prophet said the guards would take him openly.
THALABI:v10p246/r6.anchor: لأملأن عليك إن شئت هذا خيلا جردا أو رجالا مردا، فأنزل الله سبحانه فليدع ناديه أي قومه

THALABI:v10p246/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p246/r7.claim: The Prophet warned that the guards would seize Abū Jahl in full view.
THALABI:v10p246/r7.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لأخذته الزبانية

ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r1.speaker: classical commentators
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r1.claim: Commentators with a historical reading take “his council” as Mecca's pagan elders' council, dar al-nadwah.
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r1.anchor: the traditional council of elders (dar an- nadwah) in pagan Mecca

ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r2.claim: Asad more probably reads the council as the arrogance that makes people imagine themselves self-sufficient, recalling verses 6–7.
ASAD-NOTES:96:15#n9/r2.anchor: more probably, I think, it is an allusion to the arrogance which so often deludes man

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178#2/r1.claim: Nādi means the people of a gathering; al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj likewise say Abū Jahl should summon his clan or council for help.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p178#2/r1.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه. قاله (1) أبو عبيدة (2).

WAHIDI-QT:96:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:17/r1.claim: He should summon his council for help; he had threatened Muhammad with a valley full of horses and men.
WAHIDI-QT:96:17/r1.anchor: { فليدع ناديه } فليستعن بأهل مجلسه ،   وذلك أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r9.claim: The command challenges Abu Jahl to summon his assembly and seek their help; he had threatened the Messenger with a valley full of horses and men.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:9-17/r9.anchor: فليدع ناديه } فليستعن بأهل مجلسه، وذلك أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لأملأن عليك هذا الوادي

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r3.claim: Nadi derives from nadwa, a gathering for discussion; the pre-Islamic Quraysh meeting hall was Dar al-Nadwa, and the word names the assembled body, like an assembly, congress, or parliament, so “kurultay” suits contemporary Turkish.

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r4.speaker: Tirmizî
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r4.claim: Tirmidhi reports Abu Jahl’s boast that he had the majority of the assembly on his side; the verse points to this boast and answers that God will summon the Zabaniya.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r4.anchor: Tirmizî’de [5962] de rivayet olunduğu üzere Ebû Cehil, nâdîce ekseriyet kendisinin olduğunu söylediği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r1.claim: Nādī derives from consultation and means the council assembled for deliberation; Meccan consultation meetings took place at Dār al-Nadwa.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r1.anchor: “bir konuda istişare etmek üzere toplanmak” anlamına gelen nedve kökünden türemiş olup kurultayda bir araya gelen heyeti ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.speaker: Rivayete göre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.claim: After Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad while he prayed at Abraham's station and boasted of his many supporters, the verses challenged him to call his council while God would call the angels of punishment; he never dared act despite hearing them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, “O hemen kurultayını çağırsın, biz de zebânileri çağıracağız” buyurarak Hz. Peygamber’e meydan okuyan Ebû Cehil’in yetersizliğini ortaya koymak istemiştir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r1.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r1.claim: The verses about Abu Jahl calling his assembly and God calling the guards were revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl tried to stop the Prophet praying, then boasted his assembly was largest; the verses followed, and Ibn Abbas says God's guards would seize him if he summoned it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يصلي، فجاء أبو جهل

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that if Abu Jahl had called his assembly, God's guards would have seized him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والله لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله تبارك وتعالى

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.claim: The condemned is challenged to summon his earthly supporters against the punishment awaiting him, but God's summoned zabāniya outmatch that following.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die von dem Getadelten zur Hilfe gerufene Anhängerschaft (nādiyahū) wird jedoch gleich darauf durch die von Gott herbeizitierten zabāniya überboten

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.claim: The verses challenge the arrogant to summon their faction while God summons His guards; Badr later demonstrated the Quraysh’s humiliation by God’s guards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.anchor: the Quraysh was humiliated at the hands

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r2.claim: Nādī literally means a gathering or society and here denotes people linked communally, hence a group or party.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.speaker: النبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet said angels would seize Abū Jahl if he acted on his threat to trample the praying Muhammad.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال قال أبو جهل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses nādī as the man's living people or clan.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فليدع ناديه ﴾ قال قومه حية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r3.speaker: مؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r3.claim: Muʾarrij says nādī means a gathering according to Quraysh usage; the related nadā also means a council or assembly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r3.anchor: وقال مؤرج: معناه الأخذ بلغة قريش، النادي والندى: المجلس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r4.speaker: أعرابية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r4.claim: A Bedouin woman’s phrase “master of his gathering” illustrates nādī as a meeting place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الأعرابية: سيد ناديه وثمال عافيه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r5.speaker: زهير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r5.claim: Zuhayr’s verse uses andiya for assemblies visited by talk and action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r5.anchor: وقال زهير: وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم ... وأندية ينتابها القول والفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r15.claim: Nādiyahu alludes to Abu Jahl's boast that his gathering was largest in the valley; it means the people assembled there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r15.anchor: فليدع ناديه: إشارة إلى قول أبي جهل: وما بالوادي أكبر ناديا مني، والمراد أهل النادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r16.speaker: جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r16.claim: A line by Jarīr uses majlis for the people of a gathering, as its description of tawny beards and humiliation shows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r16.anchor: وقال جرير: لهم مجلس صهب السبال أذلة أي أهل مجلس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r17.claim: The command is sarcastic: Abu Jahl cannot prevail; if he summoned his circle, angels would seize him openly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r17.anchor: وهو أمر تعجبي، أي لا يقدره الله على ذلك، لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الملائكة عيانا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r1.claim: Nādī is the gathering place where people meet to converse, plural andiya; here it means the people gathered there by ellipsis, figurative attribution, or naming inhabitants by their place.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r1.anchor: النادي المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم أي يجتمعون للحديث ويجمع على أندية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r2.claim: Poetry by Jarīr or Dhū al-Rumma and by Zuhayr supports using council and gathering-place terms for the people who meet there.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r2.anchor: كما قال جرير أو ذو الرمة لهم مجلس صهب السبال أذلة سواسية أحرارها وعبيدها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r3.claim: The wording recalls the report that Abu Jahl confronted the praying Prophet and boasted that he had the largest gathering in the valley; the command taunts him by showing he can accomplish nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p187#3/r3.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى ما صح من أن أبا جهل مر برسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r1.claim: The assembly means Abu Jahl's people and clan, whom he is challenged to summon for help.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r1.anchor: قال الله عز وجل: {فليدع ناديه} أي قومه وعشيرته، أي فليستنصر بهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.claim: If Abu Jahl called his clan, God's guards would seize him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r3.claim: The offender is told to summon the people of his council to help him; a nādī is the gathering place where people confer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r3.anchor: أهل ناديه ليعينوه وهو المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r4.claim: A report says Abū Jahl confronted the praying Prophet; after the Prophet rebuked him, Abū Jahl boasted that he had the largest council in the valley, prompting the revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:15-17/r4.anchor: روي أنا أبا جهل لعنه الله مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p31/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r8.claim: النادي is the community’s gathering place and, by extension, the assembled people; نداء is the call that summons them.
BINTSHATI:v2p31/r8.anchor: والنادي في العربية: مجتمع القوم، كالندى والمنتدى. والنداء: الصوت الداعي إلى التجمع

BINTSHATI:v2p32/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r1.claim: The related terms denote a gathering and its discourse; Dar al-Nadwa was Quraysh’s council, and النادي may mean the people assembled there by local-place metaphor.
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r1.anchor: ومنه دار الندوة بمكة، كانت مجتمع قريش تقضى فيها جليل أمورها

BINTSHATI:v2p32/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r2.claim: The Quran uses the root for mutual summoning, the Day of Calling, a community gathering, and people’s assembly or social circle.

BINTSHATI:v2p32/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r3.speaker: المفسرون
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r3.claim: Exegetes connect the verse to Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad as he prayed at the Kaaba; Abu Jahl boasted that no one in the valley had a larger assembly than his.
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r3.anchor: فذكورا أن أبا جهل بن هشان حين توعد المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يطأ عنقه

BINTSHATI:v2p32/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r4.claim: The boastful person imagines his clan will support and protect him, so he persists in excess and error.
BINTSHATI:v2p32/r4.anchor: معتزاً بقومه، مدلاً ما له في عشيرته من حمى ومنعه

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.claim: The nadi is the group the deluded man summons for help; all of them are powerless against the mighty angels God summons to punish him.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.anchor: مراداً به الجمع الذين يدعوهم هذا الضال المغرور، وهو مظنه أن يؤازروه وينصروه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r1.claim: A nādī is the gathering place and the people who meet there by day; the threatened man is told to summon his associates and kin to rescue him from humiliation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r1.anchor: وأقرب من يعتز به الإنسان أهل ناديه , وهم القوم الذين يجتمعون نهارا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r2.claim: The Prophet identified Abū Jahl as the man who boasted, “You threaten me while I have the largest gathering in the valley.”
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r2.anchor: والذي نزلت فيه هو أبو جهل , قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أتهددني وأنا أكثر أهل الوادي ناديا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r14.claim: The disbelievers seek pride, independence, and status through their community, fearing the shame of becoming followers and subordinates.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r14.anchor: وكان الكفار إنما يقصدون بأعراضهم الشماخة والأنفة والعز عن أن يكونوا أتباعا أذنابا

DURR:96:6/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:6/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:6/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:6/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:6/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies Abu Jahl as forbidding Muhammad’s prayer, glosses his nadi as his clan, and says al-zabaniya are angels.
DURR:96:6/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل نهى محمداً إذا صلى { فليدع ناديه } قال : عشيرته { سندع الزبانية } قال : الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r6.speaker: أبو جهل
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r6.claim: Abu Jahl threatens to trample Muhammad's neck if he sees him praying at the Kaaba.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن عنقه

DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.claim: The Prophet says that if Abu Jahl did this, the angels would seize him in plain sight.
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.anchor: فبلغ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: لو فعل لأخذته الملائكة عيانا

DURR-FULL:v8p564/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl coming upon the Prophet praying and beginning to forbid him from it.
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل فقال: ألم أنهك عن هذا

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.claim: Abu Jahl recoils from the Prophet, seeing a trench of fire and wings; the Prophet says angels would tear him limb from limb, and the final verses identify Abu Jahl's clan and the angels as his assembly and the zabaniya.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لو دنا مني لاختطفته الملائكة عضوا عضوا

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad; the guided one is Muhammad, the denier is Abu Jahl, his assembly is his clan, and ‘zabaniya’ means police in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.claim: He identifies Abu Jahl as the one stopping Muhammad from prayer, his assembly as his clan, and the zabaniya as angels.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: أبو جهل نهى محمدا إذا صلى

TAB:96:17/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:17/r1.claim: Abu Jahl is told to summon the people of his assembly, his supporters from clan and tribe; nādī means the gathering place.
TAB:96:17/r1.anchor: فليدع أبو جهل أهل مجلسه وأنصاره

TAB:96:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Jahl threatened the Prophet while he prayed at the Maqām; God revealed the challenge, and the angels of punishment would seize Abu Jahl if he summoned his council.
TAB:96:17/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام

TAB:96:17/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r3.claim: In another report, Abu Jahl forbids the Prophet to pray and boasts of his council; after an unpreserved remark from the Prophet, Ibn Abbas says angels would seize Abu Jahl where he stood.
TAB:96:17/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

TAB:96:17/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:96:17/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl threatened to trample the praying Prophet, then recoiled, describing a fiery trench, terror, and wings; the Prophet said angels would tear him limb by limb, while attribution of the quoted revelation is uncertain.
TAB:96:17/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

TAB:96:17/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to kill Muhammad if he prayed again at the Maqām; the Prophet said battalions had darkened the space between them, and angels would seize Abu Jahl if he moved.
TAB:96:17/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه

TAB:96:17/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to step on the Prophet's neck at the Kaʿba; the Prophet said angels would take him in plain sight if he did.
TAB:96:17/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة

TAB:96:17/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the council Abu Jahl is to summon as his supporter.
TAB:96:17/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله :  {  فليدع ناديه } يقول :  فليدع ناصره

BURHAN:v2p279/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p279/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p279/r13.claim: The place name in ناديه stands for the people who gather there: this is naming the occupant by the location.
BURHAN:v2p279/r13.anchor: السادس عشر إطلاق اسم المحل على الحال

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham defines al-nādī as an assembly where people gather and decide affairs, comparing it with the Quranic reference to wrongdoing in a gathering at 29:29.
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r3.anchor: والنادي: المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه القوم ويقضون فيه أمورهم، وفي كتاب الله تعالى: وتأتون في ناديكم المنكر

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r4.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r4.claim: Ibn Hisham equates al-nādī with al-nadī, gives its plural as andiya, and explains ask the town at 12:82 to mean ask its people; 19:73 uses al-nadī.
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r4.anchor: وجمعه: أندية. فليدع أهل ناديه. كما قال تعالى: وسئل القرية

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r5.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r5.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r5.claim: Ubayd ibn al-Abras's verse uses al-nadī and al-nādī in praising the people of his assembly, as poetic evidence for the gathering sense.

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r6.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r6.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r6.claim: Salama ibn Jandal's verse uses andiya for assemblies, supporting the plural of al-nādī.

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r7.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r7.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r7.claim: Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd's line uses al-nadā while describing the assembly, another poetic attestation for the term.

ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r1.claim: Al-nādī and al-nadā mean an assembly or meeting place; an Arab woman’s phrase and Zuhayr’s verse using andiya provide usage evidence.
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r1.anchor: النادي والندى : المجلس ، ومنه قول الأعرابية : سيد ناديه وثمال عافيه ، وقال زهير : وفيهم مقامات حسان وجوههم

ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r2.speaker: جرير
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r2.claim: Jarīr’s line illustrates al-majlis for the people assembled there: “red-mustached, humble” describes the attendees, not the venue.
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r2.anchor: وقال جرير : لهم مجلس صهب السبال أذلة . . . أي أهل مجلس ، ولذلك وصف بقوله : صهب السبال أذلة

ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r3.claim: The phrase alludes to Abū Jahl’s boast that no one in the valley had a larger council; “his council” means the people in it.
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى قول أبي جهل : وما بالوادي أكبر نادياً مني ، والمراد أهل النادي

ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r4.claim: The command is an exclamatory challenge: God will not enable him, and if he summons his council, the angels will seize him openly.
ABUHAYYAN:96:17/r4.anchor: وهو أمر تعجبي ، أي لا يقدره الله على ذلك ، لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الملائكة عياناً

ALUSI:96:17/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:17/r1.claim: Nādin is the council where a group gathers to converse, with plural andiya; the command can mean summon the people of his council, or use the place for its occupants by metonymy.
ALUSI:96:17/r1.anchor: النادي المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم أي يجتمعون للحديث ويجمع على أندية

ALUSI:96:17/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:17/r2.speaker: جرير أو ذو الرمة
ALUSI:96:17/r2.claim: A line attributed uncertainly to Jarīr or Dhū al-Rumma uses majlis for its assembled occupants; Zuhayr's cited line likewise uses andiya as gathering places where speech and action occur.
ALUSI:96:17/r2.anchor: كما قال جرير أو ذو الرمة

ALUSI:96:17/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:17/r3.speaker: زهير
ALUSI:96:17/r3.claim: Zuhayr's poetry cites andiya as places frequented by speech and action, supporting the sense of gathering places.

ALUSI:96:17/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:17/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:17/r4.claim: A sound report says Abū Jahl challenged the Prophet while he prayed, saying he had forbidden him and that he had the largest council in the valley.
ALUSI:96:17/r4.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى ما صح من أن أبا جهل مر برسول الله

ALUSI:96:17/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:17/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:96:17/r5.claim: Al-Baḥr reads the imperative as a challenge that exposes Abū Jahl's inability to accomplish anything.
ALUSI:96:17/r5.anchor: للتعجيز والإشارة إلى أنه لا يقدر على شيء

BAGHAWI:96:17/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:17/r1.claim: His assembly means his people and clan, whom he is told to call for help.
BAGHAWI:96:17/r1.anchor: أي قومه وعشيرته ، أي فليستنصر بهم

BAYDAWI:96:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:17/r1.claim: He is told to call the people of his assembly so they can help him.
BAYDAWI:96:17/r1.anchor: { فليدع نادية } أي أهل ناديه ليعينوه

BAYDAWI:96:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:17/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:17/r2.claim: A nādī is the council or gathering place where people sit together.
BAYDAWI:96:17/r2.anchor: وهو المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم

BIQAI:96:17/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:17/r1.claim: A nadī is the person's daytime gathering and its members, who talk and find fellowship; a person relies most readily on these companions and clan for pride and support.
BIQAI:96:17/r1.anchor: وهم القوم الذين يجتمعون نهاراً ليحدث بعضهم بعضاً

BIQAI:96:17/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:17/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:17/r2.claim: Biqāʿī identifies the target as Abū Jahl, who challenged Muhammad by boasting that he had the largest gathering in the valley; the command is to summon those supporters for rescue.
BIQAI:96:17/r2.anchor: والذي نزلت فيه هو أبو جهل

DURR:96:17/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:17/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of worldly gain are both insatiable: knowledge brings God’s approval, while wealth-seeking leads to transgression.
DURR:96:17/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:17/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Abū Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad’s neck at the Kaʿba; the Prophet said angels would seize him in plain sight if he did.
DURR:96:17/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت محمداً يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن عنقه

DURR:96:17/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abū Jahl confronted the Prophet at prayer, boasted of having the largest council, and the verses answered that his council and God’s angels would be summoned; Abū Jahl would be seized.
DURR:96:17/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي ، فجاء أبو جهل فقال

DURR:96:17/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the Maqām; when asked why he did not act, the Prophet said the space between them had darkened, and angels would seize him if he moved.
DURR:96:17/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه

DURR:96:17/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r5.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
DURR:96:17/r5.claim: Al-ʿAbbās says Abū Jahl vowed to trample the Prophet while prostrating; when Muhammad recited the sūra, Abū Jahl said the sky’s horizon was blocked from him, and Muhammad prostrated at its end.
DURR:96:17/r5.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب قال : كنت يوماً في المسجد فأقبل أبو جهل

DURR:96:17/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:96:17/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl recoiled from the praying Prophet, describing a trench of fire and wings between them; Muhammad said angels would tear him limb from limb if he approached.
DURR:96:17/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه إلا بين أظهركم ؟

DURR:96:17/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:96:17/r7.claim: In Abū Hurayra’s report, the condemned man is Abū Jahl, his “council” is his people, and the zabāniya are angels.
DURR:96:17/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه إلا بين أظهركم ؟

DURR:96:17/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies Abū Jahl as the man who forbade prayer and says he threw camel entrails onto Muhammad’s back as he prostrated.
DURR:96:17/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل بن هشام

DURR:96:17/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:17/r9.claim: Qatāda says the passage was revealed over Abū Jahl’s threat against Muhammad: the guided man is Muhammad, the denier is Abū Jahl, his council is his people and clan, and zabāniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:17/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:17/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:17/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies the forbidding man as Abū Jahl, his nadi as his clan, and the zabāniya as angels.
DURR:96:17/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل نهى محمداً إذا صلى

DURR:96:17/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “we will seize him by the forelock” as “we will take him.”
DURR:96:17/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { لنسفعن } قال : لنأخذن .

DURR:96:17/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:96:17/r12.claim: ʿIkrima gives the same gloss: “we will take him.”

DURR:96:18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:18/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Abū Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad’s neck at the Kaʿba; the Prophet said angels would seize him in plain sight if he did.

DURR:96:18/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:18/r9.claim: Qatāda says the passage was revealed over Abū Jahl’s threat against Muhammad: the guided man is Muhammad, the denier is Abū Jahl, his council is his people and clan, and zabāniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:18/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:18/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:18/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies the forbidding man as Abū Jahl, his nadi as his clan, and the zabāniya as angels.
DURR:96:18/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل نهى محمداً إذا صلى

DURR:96:18/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:18/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “we will seize him by the forelock” as “we will take him.”
DURR:96:18/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { لنسفعن } قال : لنأخذن .

DURR:96:18/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r12.speaker: عكرمة
DURR:96:18/r12.claim: ʿIkrima gives the same gloss: “we will take him.”

IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.claim: The general statement that humans transgress when they feel self-sufficient introduces the specific account of the prohibitor, encompassing the challenge through Abū Jahl's invitation to his assembly.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.anchor: فموقع قوله :  { إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى } موقع المقدمة لما يرد بعده من قوله :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى

IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī transmit Ibn ʿAbbās's report: Abū Jahl confronted the Prophet praying at the Maqām, threatened him, claimed the valley's largest assembly, and the two verses exposed his intent to summon supporters against him.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.anchor: ومناسبة ذلك ما رواه الترمذي والنسائي عن ابن عباس قال :  « كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل

IBNASHUR:96:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r2.claim: Nādī first names the place where people assemble; the related nadwah means a group, and a place is called a nādī only while the people are gathered there.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r2.anchor: والنادي :  اسم للمكان الذي يجتمع فيه القوم .  يقال :  ندا القوم نَدْواً ،  إذ اجتمعوا .  والندوة

IBNASHUR:96:17/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r3.claim: Nādī can also mean the people who gather there, which is Abū Jahl's sense: he claims many followers and presents himself as a leader to whom people turn.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r3.anchor: ويطلق النادي على الذين ينتدون فيه وهو معنى قول أبي جهل :  إني لأكثر أهل هذا الوادي نادياً ،  أي ناساً يجلسون إليَّ

IBNASHUR:96:17/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r4.claim: The assembly is called a nādī by day; its nighttime equivalent is al-musāmir, as in the Qurʾānic phrase samiran tahjurūn.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r4.anchor: ويقال النادي لمجلس القوم نهاراً ،  فأما مجلسهم في الليل فيسمى المسامر قال تعالى :  { سامراً تهجرون }

IBNASHUR:96:17/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r5.claim: Quṣayy built Dār al-Nadwah near the Sacred Mosque for Quraysh's consultations and affairs, marriage contracts, and dressing girls in shirts to announce puberty.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r5.anchor: واتخذ قصي لندوة قريش داراً تسمى دار الندوة حول المسجد الحرام وجعلها لتشاورهم ومهماتهم وفيها يعقد على الأزواج

IBNASHUR:96:17/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r6.claim: Khayzurān later bought the house; mosque expansions incorporated parts under ʿAbd al-Malik and al-Manṣūr, al-Mahdī lodged in its remainder in AH 160, and King Saʿūd incorporated the site in AH 1379.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r6.anchor: وهذه الدار كانت اشترتها الخيزران زوجة المنصور أبي جعفر وأدخلتها في ساحة المسجد الحرام ،  وأدخل بعضها في المسجد الحرام

IBNASHUR:96:17/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r7.claim: Calling a group's members by the place where they meet parallels asking a town for its people in 12:82 and poetic uses of majlis, maqām, and majmaʿ by Dhū al-Rummah, Zuhayr, and Labīd.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r7.anchor: وإطلاق النادي على أهله نظير إطلاق القرية على أهلها في قوله تعالى :  { واسأل القرية }  [ يوسف :  82 ] ونظير إطلاق المجلس على أهله

IBNASHUR:96:17/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r8.claim: The imperative is a challenge: if Abū Jahl summons his assembly to assault the Prophet, God will summon angels to destroy them; it is a Qurʾānic miracle that neither Abū Jahl nor his hearers dared act after hearing it.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r8.anchor: ولام الأمر في { فليدع ناديه } للتعجيز لأن أبا جهل هدد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بكثرة أنصاره وهم أهل ناديه

IBNASHUR:96:17/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:17/r9.claim: The assembly is annexed to Abū Jahl because he is its chief and its members gather around him, as an Arab woman called a man the master and support of his assembly.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r9.anchor: وإضافة النادي إلى ضميره لأنه رئيسهم ويجتمعون إليه قالت أعرابية :  « سيد ناديه ،  وثمال عافيهْ »

IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.claim: Kallā cancels the suggestion that Abū Jahl can summon his assembly, reinforcing the preceding challenge that he will not carry it out.
IBNASHUR:96:19/r1.anchor: و { كَلاّ } ردع لإِبطال ما تضمنه قوله :  { فليدع ناديه } ،  أي وليس بفاعل

IBNATIYYA:96:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:17/r1.claim: The command refers to Abu Jahl’s boast that no one in the valley had a larger council than he did.
IBNATIYYA:96:17/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فليدع نادية } إشارة إلى قول أبي جهل : وما بالوادي أكثر نادياً مني

IBNATIYYA:96:17/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:17/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:17/r2.claim: Nādī and nadī mean an assembly while people are gathered; the verse of Zuhayr and an Arab woman's phrase illustrate the usage.
IBNATIYYA:96:17/r2.anchor: والنادي والندي المجلس ، ومنه دار الندوة ، ومنه قول زهير

IBNKATHIR:96:17/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:17/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:17/r1.claim: The council is the man's people and clan, whom he is challenged to call for support.
IBNKATHIR:96:17/r1.anchor: أي : قومه وعشيرته ، أي : ليدعهم يستنصر بهم

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.claim: In another Ibn Abbas report, Abu Jahl threatens the Prophet at the Maqam and boasts of his large council; Ibn Abbas says angels would seize the council immediately. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل بن هشام

MAWARDI:96:17/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:17/r1.claim: The command is directed at Abu Jahl.
MAWARDI:96:17/r1.anchor: يعني أبا جهل ، والنادي مجلس أهل الندى والجود

MAWARDI:96:17/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:17/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:17/r2.claim: Nadi is the gathering of people known for generosity.

MAWARDI:96:17/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:17/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:17/r3.claim: He is told to summon the people of his council, whether his clan or a supporter.
MAWARDI:96:17/r3.anchor: ومعنى " فليدع ناديه " أي فليدع أهل ناديه من عشيرة أو نصير

NASAFI:96:17/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:17/r1.claim: The nādī is the meeting place where a group gathers; here it means the people who gather there.
NASAFI:96:17/r1.anchor: النادي المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه القوم

NASAFI:96:17/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:17/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:17/r2.claim: A report says Abū Jahl found the Prophet praying, challenged him for ignoring his prohibition, and boasted that he had the largest gathering in the valley; the passage was revealed then.
NASAFI:96:17/r2.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل مر بالنبي عليه السلام وهو يصلي

NASAFI:96:18/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:18/r1.claim: The nādī is the meeting place where a group gathers; here it means the people who gather there.
NASAFI:96:18/r1.anchor: النادي المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه القوم

NASAFI:96:18/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:18/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:18/r2.claim: A report says Abū Jahl found the Prophet praying, challenged him for ignoring his prohibition, and boasted that he had the largest gathering in the valley; the passage was revealed then.
NASAFI:96:18/r2.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل مر بالنبي عليه السلام وهو يصلي

QURTUBI:96:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:17/r1.claim: Nādī means the gathering and, by extension, its people and the man’s clan, whom he is challenged to call for help.
QURTUBI:96:17/r1.anchor: أي أهل مجلسه وعشيرته ،   فليستنصر بهم

QURTUBI:96:17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:17/r10.claim: A report says Abu Jahl boasted he would summon his people after hearing the threat to seize his forelock; hearing of the zabāniya frightened him, and he claimed to have seen a threatening horseman.
QURTUBI:96:17/r10.anchor: وروي في الخبر أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لما قرأ هذه السورة

QURTUBI:96:17/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:96:17/r16.claim: Via ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet at the Maqām, boasted of his large assembly, and the verses were revealed; had he summoned it, the zabāniya would have seized him immediately. Al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ.
QURTUBI:96:17/r16.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : مر أبو جهل على النبي

QURTUBI:96:17/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:17/r17.claim: In Arabic, nādī is the meeting place where people gather, with the intended reference here to the people present.
QURTUBI:96:17/r17.anchor: والنادي في كلام العرب : المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم ،   أي يجتمعون

QURTUBI:96:17/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r18.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI:96:17/r18.claim: The line using majlis illustrates the meeting-place sense of nādī.
QURTUBI:96:17/r18.anchor: كما قال جرير : لهم مجلسٌ صُهْبُ السِّبَالِ أذِلَّةٌ

QURTUBI:96:17/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r19.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI:96:17/r19.claim: Zuhayr’s maqāmāt and andiya illustrate that these words refer to assemblies.
QURTUBI:96:17/r19.anchor: وقال زهير : وفيهمْ مقاماتٌ حسان وُجُوههم

QURTUBI:96:17/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r20.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI:96:17/r20.claim: The cited verse uses al-majlis for an assembly, supporting the meeting-place sense.
QURTUBI:96:17/r20.anchor: وقال آخر : واستبَّ بعدك يا كُلَيْبُ المجلِسُ

QURTUBI:96:17/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r21.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI:96:17/r21.claim: The verb nādaytu means to sit with someone, as Zuhayr’s phrase about a man who sits with the tribe shows.
QURTUBI:96:17/r21.anchor: وقد ناديت الرجل أناديه إذا جالسته

QURTUBI:96:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:18/r1.speaker: author

QURTUBI:96:18/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:18/r10.claim: A report says Abu Jahl boasted he would summon his people after hearing the threat to seize his forelock; hearing of the zabāniya frightened him, and he claimed to have seen a threatening horseman.
QURTUBI:96:18/r10.anchor: وروي في الخبر أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لما قرأ هذه السورة

QURTUBI:96:18/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:18/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:96:18/r16.claim: Via ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet at the Maqām, boasted of his large assembly, and the verses were revealed; had he summoned it, the zabāniya would have seized him immediately. Al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ.
QURTUBI:96:18/r16.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : مر أبو جهل على النبي

QURTUBI:96:18/r17.anchor: والنادي في كلام العرب : المجلس الذي ينتدي فيه القوم ،   أي يجتمعون

QURTUBI:96:18/r18.speaker: جرير

QURTUBI:96:18/r18.anchor: كما قال جرير : لهم مجلسٌ صُهْبُ السِّبَالِ أذِلَّةٌ

QURTUBI:96:18/r19.anchor: وقال زهير : وفيهمْ مقاماتٌ حسان وُجُوههم

QURTUBI:96:18/r20.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI:96:18/r20.claim: The cited verse uses al-majlis for an assembly, supporting the meeting-place sense.
QURTUBI:96:18/r20.anchor: وقال آخر : واستبَّ بعدك يا كُلَيْبُ المجلِسُ

QURTUBI:96:18/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:18/r21.speaker: زهير
QURTUBI:96:18/r21.claim: The verb nādaytu means to sit with someone, as Zuhayr’s phrase about a man who sits with the tribe shows.
QURTUBI:96:18/r21.anchor: وقد ناديت الرجل أناديه إذا جالسته

RAZI:96:16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r3.speaker: أبو جهل
RAZI:96:16/r3.claim: After Muhammad spoke sharply and recited the verses, Abu Jahl boasted that he had the largest assembly in the valley; the following threat to summon angels answered his boast.
RAZI:96:16/r3.anchor: قال : يا محمد بمن تهددني وأني لأكثر هذا الوادي ناديا ، فافتخر بجماعته الذين كانوا يأكلون حطامه ، فنزل قوله تعالى : { فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية }

RAZI:96:16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI:96:16/r4.claim: Al-Nādī means the people of the gathering, not its venue; a place is not called a nādī unless its people are present. The term is linked to assembly, as at Mecca's Dār al-Nadwa for consultation.
RAZI:96:16/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : ناديه أي أهل مجلسه

RAZI:96:16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r5.claim: Another derivation calls it the gathering-place of generosity; the wording sarcastically invites Abu Jahl to assemble his supposedly generous defenders.
RAZI:96:16/r5.anchor: وقيل : سمي ناديا لأنه مجلس الندى والجود

RAZI:96:16/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r11.claim: One reading challenges Abu Jahl to call his allies against Muhammad: God will summon angels beyond the assembly's power.
RAZI:96:16/r11.anchor: ( الأول ) : أي فليفعل ما ذكره من أنه يدعو أنصاره

RAZI:96:16/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:96:16/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that if Abu Jahl called his assembly, the angels would seize him immediately, in full view.
RAZI:96:16/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية

RAZI:96:16/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r13.claim: Another explanation says the threat foretells Abu Jahl being dragged like a dog in this life, as happened at Badr.
RAZI:96:16/r13.anchor: وقيل : هذا إخبار من الله تعالى بأنه يجر في الدنيا

RAZI:96:16/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r14.claim: A further explanation places the angels' dragging of Abu Jahl into Hell in the afterlife.
RAZI:96:16/r14.anchor: وقيل : بل هذا إخبار بأن الزبانية يجرونه في الآخرة إلى النار

RAZI:96:16/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r15.claim: A second interpretation rearranges the sequence: God seizes the forelock and summons angels in the afterlife, then Abu Jahl calls his assembly to protect him.
RAZI:96:16/r15.anchor: ( القول الثاني ) : أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا أي لنسفعا بالناصية

RAZI:96:17/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:17/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:17/r1.claim: The fa in “let him call his assembly” marks a miracle: the challenge invites Abu Jahl to act, but he dared not, confirming the Prophet's miracle.
RAZI:96:17/r1.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : الفاء في قوله : { فليدع ناديه } تدل على المعجز
